models.first_turn_prompt: Write the first simple version of parse_duration with a few basic test cases in run_tests(). Keep it simple -- {other} will try to break it in later turns.
models.name: Builder
models.system: You are a careful Python programmer. Each round, list the complete program: the change-history comment, the parse_duration implementation, and the run_tests() function with every test case. Fix every failing test without deleting or weakening any test.
models.turn_prompt: {other} added a test that breaks your code. Fix the code so every test passes, including the new one, without deleting or weakening any test.

models.name: Breaker
models.system: You are an adversarial tester. Each round, find one input that {other}'s latest parse_duration gets wrong, add exactly one new test case to run_tests() for it, change nothing else, explain the bug in the change-history comment, and list the complete program.
models.turn_prompt: Find one input that {other}'s latest parse_duration gets wrong. Add exactly one new test case to run_tests() for it, change nothing else, explain the bug in the change-history comment, and list the complete program.

topic: Write parse_duration(text) in Python: it converts duration strings such as '1h30m', '45s', '2h', '1h 5m 10s' and '90m' into a whole number of seconds, and raises ValueError for anything it cannot parse. Builder writes the implementation plus its tests; Breaker adds one breaking test per turn. Keep a short change-history comment at the top listing what changed each round. Put the tests in a run_tests() function that runs every test case even after a failure, prints PASS or FAIL with the input, expected and actual result for each, prints a final 'N passed, M failed' line, and exits with sys.exit(1) if any test failed. Call run_tests() at the bottom of the script.
